## Policies (M1 and A1) {#sec-ov-policies}

The policies block turns the inputs of a scenario into **price signals**: a rate per tonne of CO2 or per unit of
fuel, for each year, sector and fuel. Every later block reads these signals. Prices add them to the retail price
(@sec-prices); fuel use and power respond to the price and to the shadow price (@sec-demand, @sec-power); revenues
collect them (@sec-fiscal). The block depends on no model quantity, so it is computed for all years in the prepare
stage.

The methodology describes the policy options in its user guide
([methodology, section 1.3.2.3](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/01_User_Guide.html#overview-of-policies-accounted-for-in-cpat))
and the price notation in
[methodology, section 3.2.2](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#sec-PricesNotation).

### The instruments at a glance {#sec-ov-instruments}

| Instrument | Acts through | Raises revenue | Main inputs | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Carbon tax | Fuel price (per tCO2 × emission factor) | Yes | `CPIntro`, `CPOutro`, `CPLevelStart`, `CPLevelTarget`, coverage `MCov*` | @sec-ov-carbon-tax |
| New ETS | Fuel price (auctioned part) and shadow price (free part) | Auctioned part | `NewETS`, `ETSIntro`, `ETSOutro`, cap, auction shares, coverage `ETSCov*` | @sec-ov-ets |
| Feebates | Shadow price (efficiency margin) | No (revenue neutral) | `FeebateIntro`, `FeebateOutro`, rates by group, coverage `FbCov*` | @sec-ov-shadow |
| Regulations | Shadow price (efficiency margin) | No | `ScenarioSelected`, efficiency adjustments `SPPEffAdj*` | @sec-ov-shadow |
| Fuel excises (fuel price reform) | Fuel price (per price unit) | Yes | `FprIntro`, `FprOutro`, `FprStart*`, `FprFinal*` | @sec-ov-excise |
| Consumer subsidy and price-control phase-outs | Fuel price (wedges) | Yes (subsidy saved) | `ConsSubPha`, `PrcContPha`, years, periods, shares | @sec-ov-phaseouts |
| Producer subsidy reform | Supply cost | Yes (subsidy saved) | `ProdSubPh`, year, period, share, scope by fuel | @sec-ov-producer |
| Methane fee | Methane abatement | Yes | `MPIntro`, `MPOutro`, `MPLevelStart`, `MPLevelTarget`, `CTforMethane` | @sec-ov-methane |
| Existing carbon pricing | Change in the fuel price against the price data | Yes | `ExistingCTApply`, `ExistingETSApply`, growth rates | @sec-ov-existing |

Power-sector policies (renewable subsidies, PPAs, rebates, new investment bans, the electricity excise) are set in
the same scenario column and explained in @sec-power; road vehicle policies (vehicle feebates, EV subsidies,
purchase taxes, distance taxes) in @sec-transport; revenue recycling in @sec-fiscal and @sec-distribution.

### The policy path {#sec-ov-path}

Every policy is a **path from a start year to a target year**, set per scenario: zero before the start year, linear
from a start level to a target level, and then either held or continued ([M1.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-1)).

$$
\Lambda(t;\, T_0, T_1, x_0, x_1) = \begin{cases} 0 & t < T_0 \\[4pt] x_0 + (x_1 - x_0)\,\dfrac{t - T_0}{\max(T_1 - T_0,\,1)} & t \ge T_0 \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ov-path}

where

- $T_0$ is the start year and $T_1$ the target year of the policy (inputs);
- $x_0$ is the level in the start year and $x_1$ the level in the target year (inputs);
- $\max(T_1 - T_0, 1)$ guards against a target year equal to the start year.

$\Lambda$ **continues the line** after $T_1$. The path **held flat** after the target year reads the line at
$\min(t, T_1)$:

$$
\bar{\Lambda}(t;\, T_0, T_1, x_0, x_1) = \Lambda\big(\min(t, T_1);\, T_0, T_1, x_0, x_1\big) \quad \text{for } t \ge T_0
$$ {#eq-ov-path-flat}

and 0 before $T_0$. Which form a policy takes after its target year:

| Path | After the target year | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| Carbon price | Continues the line if `ExtendCarbonPriceBeyondOutro` = Linear*; otherwise held flat | Scenario input |
| Fuel price reform (excises) | Linear* continues the line; Percentage grows at the path's average annual rate; otherwise held | `ExtendCarbonPriceBeyondOutro` (the same input) |
| Feebate rates | Held flat | Fixed |
| ETS benchmarks and cap change | Held flat; the cap itself is held at its last level if `ETSCapCont` = Constant | Fixed; scenario input |
| Methane fee | Continues the line | Fixed |
| Exemption phase-out, subsidy phase-outs | Reach their end share and stay there | Fixed |

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: the policy path"}
```
def path(t, t0, t1, x0, x1, hold=True):
    if t < t0:
        return 0
    tt = min(t, t1) if hold else t          # hold: flat after the target year
    return x0 + (x1 - x0) / max(t1 - t0, 1) * (tt - t0)
```
:::

### Carbon tax {#sec-ov-carbon-tax}

The carbon tax is a charge per tonne of CO2 on the fuels and sectors it covers. It is added to the fuel price as
the rate times the fuel's emission factor (@sec-prices). The methodology's notation is $NCT$ for the new carbon tax
and $\varphi_{NCT}$ for its coverage
([methodology, section 3.9.3.1.1](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#policy-coverage-and-exemptions)).

**The carbon price path.** The national carbon price follows the policy path, made real if the inputs are nominal
([M1.2](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-2)):

$$
\tau_t = \Lambda^{*}(t;\, T^{cp}_0, T^{cp}_1, x^{cp}_0, x^{cp}_1)\; n_t, \qquad n_t = \begin{cases} \nu_t & \text{inputs nominal} \\ 1 & \text{inputs real} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ov-cptraj}

where

- $\tau_t$ (`cptraj`, methodology $NCT_t$) is the carbon price in real USD/tCO2;
- $\Lambda^{*}$ is $\Lambda$ if `ExtendCarbonPriceBeyondOutro` = Linear*, else $\bar{\Lambda}$;
- $T^{cp}_0$, $T^{cp}_1$ are `CPIntro`, `CPOutro`; $x^{cp}_0$, $x^{cp}_1$ are `CPLevelStart`, `CPLevelTarget`;
- $n_t$ (`cp.nom`) is the CPI index $\nu_t$ if `NomorReal` starts with "Nominal", else 1 (default Real*).

**Explicit or shadow pricing.** The input `ScenarioSelected` picks a *main scenario* from the legacy table of main
scenarios. It says whether the carbon price path is an explicit tax or a shadow price
(@sec-ov-shadow). The explicit carbon price is

$$
\tau^{x}_t = \tau_t\; \mathbb{1}[\text{main scenario prices explicitly}]
$$ {#eq-ov-cpx}

(`cpx`, `cp.exp`). A text that is not in the table counts as explicit pricing, as the shipped " - Carbon tax".

**Coverage by fuel and by sector.** The tax covers a fuel and a sector through two sets of switches, one per fuel
(`MCovCoa`, ..., `MCovOop`; biomass `CTaxCoversBiomass`; jet fuel reads the kerosene switch) and one per coverage
sector (`MCovPow`, `MCovRod`, ..., `MCovOen`). Unticked fuels and sectors are exempt. An exemption can be phased
out: in a policy scenario with `ExemptPhaseout` = TRUE, an uncovered fuel or sector becomes taxed linearly over
`ExemptPhaseoutPeriod` years from `YearPha`:

$$
\varphi_{t} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{switch ticked} \\[4pt] \mathbb{1}[o \ne B]\;\mathbb{1}[\text{ExemptPhaseout}]\;\mathbb{1}[t \ge T^{cp}_0]\;\min\!\left(\max\!\left(\dfrac{t + 1 - T^{pha}}{N^{pha}},\, 0\right),\, 1\right) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ov-coverage}

where

- $\varphi_t$ (`ctcov`) is the coverage of one fuel ($\varphi_{NCT,f}$) or one sector ($\varphi_{NCT,s}$), a share;
- $T^{pha}$ is `YearPha`, $N^{pha}$ is `ExemptPhaseoutPeriod`;
- the phase-out share itself is `exph`.

A fuel used in a sector is taxed by the product of the two coverages: the sector coverage enters the rate by sector
below, the fuel coverage the rate per GJ ([M2.4](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M2-4), @sec-prices).

**The rate by sector.** Where the new ETS covers a sector, the ETS replaces the carbon tax. The carbon tax rate of
coverage sector $s$ is ([M1.3](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-3)):

$$
T_{s,t} = \tau^{x}_t\; c_{s,t}\; (1 - \kappa_{s,t}), \qquad c_{s,t} = \begin{cases} 1 - \text{xcov}_{j(s),\min(t, T_x)} & \text{tax complementary to an existing ETS} \\ \varphi_{NCT,s,t} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ov-ctr}

where

- $T_{s,t}$ (`ctr`, methodology $NCT_{s,t}$) is the carbon tax rate of sector $s$ in USD/tCO2;
- $\kappa_{s,t}$ is the new ETS coverage of the sector (@eq-ov-ets-coverage);
- $c_{s,t}$ is the sector coverage of the tax. If `CTaxComplimentaryToETS` = Yes, the new tax covers what the
  country's existing national ETS does not: one minus the existing ETS coverage $\text{xcov}$ of the sector's ECP
  sector $j(s)$ in the data year of $t$. Otherwise new instruments add to existing ones.

**Residential LPG and kerosene.** With `AlwaysExemptResLPGKer` = Yes (default No*), the new carbon tax, the new ETS
cost and the new excise of residential LPG and kerosene are zero. The model applies this through an **exemption
factor** $x_{s,f}$ (`exf`) that multiplies each new policy per unit of fuel:

$$
x_{s,f} = \begin{cases} 0 & f \in \{\text{LPG, kerosene}\},\ s = \text{residential},\ \text{switch Yes} \\ 1 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ov-exf}

Existing taxes, existing carbon pricing and subsidy phase-outs still apply to these fuels, and the shadow price is
not exempted (@sec-prices).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: carbon tax"}
```
for t in years:
    tt = t if ExtendCarbonPriceBeyondOutro == 'Linear*' else min(t, CPOutro)
    cp_nom[t] = infl[t] if NomorReal.startswith('Nominal') else 1
    cptraj[t] = 0 if t < CPIntro else (CPLevelStart + (CPLevelTarget - CPLevelStart)
                                       / max(CPOutro - CPIntro, 1) * (tt - CPIntro)) * cp_nom[t]
    cpx[t] = cptraj[t] * explicit(ScenarioSelected)          # 1 unless a shadow-pricing scenario
    exph[t] = 0
    if scenario > 1 and ExemptPhaseout and t >= CPIntro:
        exph[t] = clip((t + 1 - YearPha) / ExemptPhaseoutPeriod, 0, 1)
    for x in fuels + coverage_sectors:                        # MCov* switches
        ctcov[x][t] = 1 if switch[x] else exph[t]
    for s in coverage_sectors:
        if CTaxComplimentaryToETS starts with 'Yes':
            cover = 1 - existing_ets_coverage[ecp_sector(s)][min(t, last_ecp_year)]
        else:
            cover = ctcov[s][t]
        ctr[s][t] = cpx[t] * cover * (1 - etsc[s][t])
exf['all'] = 1
exf['res'] = 0 if AlwaysExemptResLPGKer starts with 'Yes' else 1   # read by residential LPG and kerosene
```
:::

### New emissions trading system {#sec-ov-ets}

A new ETS sets a **cap** on the emissions of the sectors it covers. The model does not clear the permit market
inside a run: it estimates the permit price that would meet the cap, applies it like a carbon tax, and reports how
far emissions end up from the cap. A goal seek outside the run then refines the price (@sec-emissions). The
methodology's user guide describes the option in
[methodology, section 1.3.2.4.2](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/01_User_Guide.html#emission-trading-systems).

**On and coverage.** The ETS applies from its start year if `NewETS` = Yes; it covers the sectors whose switch
(`ETSCovPow`, ..., `ETSCovOen`) is ticked:

$$
\text{on}_t = \mathbb{1}[\text{NewETS}]\;\mathbb{1}[t \ge T^{E}_0], \qquad \kappa_{s,t} = \text{on}_t\;\mathbb{1}[\text{ETS covers } s]
$$ {#eq-ov-ets-coverage}

where $T^{E}_0$ is `ETSIntro` and $\kappa_{s,t}$ (`etsc`) the effective coverage of sector $s$.

**Free allocation.** Part of the permits can be allocated free, in proportion to output (output-based
allocation, OBR). The benchmark of a group is the share of its emission intensity allocated free; it runs from one
minus the auctioned share at the start year to one minus the auctioned share at the target year, and is held after:

$$
B_{G,t} = \bar{\Lambda}\big(t;\, T^{E}_0, T^{E}_1,\, 1 - a_0,\, 1 - a_1\big), \qquad \omega_{s,t} = \min\big(1, \max(0, B_{G(s),t})\big)
$$ {#eq-ov-ets-benchmark}

where

- $B_{G,t}$ (`etsb`) is the benchmark of ETS group $G$ (power, transport, residential, industry);
- $a_0$, $a_1$ are `ETSAuctStart`, `ETSAuctTarget`, the same for every group (default: nothing auctioned, so
  $B = 1$);
- $T^{E}_1$ is `ETSOutro`;
- $\omega_{s,t}$ (`obr`) is the OBR share of sector $s$, the benchmark of its group $G(s)$ bounded to $[0, 1]$.

**The cap.** The cap is a change against the baseline emissions of the covered sectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathit{bce}_t &= \sum_s \mathit{CO2}^{B}_{s,t}\;\kappa_{s,t} \\
\mathit{chg}_t &= \bar{\Lambda}\big(t;\, T^{E}_0, T^{E}_1,\, \mathit{chg}_0,\, \mathit{chg}_1\big) \\
\mathit{cap}_t &= \begin{cases} \mathit{cap}_{t-1} & t > T^{E}_1 \text{ and the cap is held Constant} \\ \text{on}_t\; \mathit{bce}_t\,(1 + \mathit{chg}_t) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ov-ets-cap}

where

- $\mathit{bce}_t$ (`ets.bce`, MtCO2) is the baseline covered emissions;
- $\mathit{CO2}^{B}_{s,t}$ (`bco2`) is the baseline CO2 of ETS sector $s$, stored from scenario 1 as data;
- $\mathit{chg}_0$, $\mathit{chg}_1$ are `ETSChangeRelStart`, `ETSChangeRelTarget` (for example $-0.05$ and $-0.20$);
- `ETSCapCont` = Constant holds the cap at its last level after the target year (and only while the ETS is on);
  otherwise the relative change is held.

**Volatility.** A volatile permit price raises the cost of abatement: firms act as if the price were lower. The
**volatility adjustment** converts the permit price into a tax-equivalent price:

$$
V = \frac{1 + r\, i}{1 + v\, i}
$$ {#eq-ov-ets-vadj}

where

- $V$ (`ets.vadj`) is the tax-equivalent price per USD of permit price;
- $v$ (`ets.vol`) is the assumed annual price volatility of the ETS, and $i$ (`ets.imp`) the abatement-cost
  increase per unit of volatility, both read by label from the table below;
- $r$ is the carbon tax policy risk (`ETSCTRisk`, 0.2).

| Label (`ETSVolatility`, `ETSVolImpact`) | Medium* | High | Low | Zero |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Volatility $v$ | 0.42 | 0.63 | 0.28 | 0 |
| Impact $i$ | 0.5 | 0.75 | 0.333 | 0 |

At Medium, $V = (1 + 0.2 \times 0.5)/(1 + 0.42 \times 0.5) = 1/1.1$.

**The fast price estimate.** With one semi-elasticity of covered emissions to the price, the price that brings
covered emissions from $bce$ to the cap solves $cap = bce\; e^{\bar{\sigma} V p}$
([A1.1](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A1-1)):

$$
\bar{\sigma}_t = \frac{\sum_s \mathit{CO2}^{B}_{s,t}\,\kappa_{s,t}\,\sigma_s\,\big(1 - (1 - \vartheta)\,\omega_{s,t}\big)}{\mathit{bce}_t}
$$ {#eq-ov-ets-se}

$$
\hat{p}_t = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\ln(\mathit{cap}_t / \mathit{bce}_t)}{\bar{\sigma}_t\, V} & \text{on}_t = 1,\ 0 < \mathit{cap}_t < \mathit{bce}_t,\ \bar{\sigma}_t < 0 \\[8pt] 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ov-ets-est}

where

- $\bar{\sigma}_t$ (`ets.se`, per USD/tCO2) is the effective semi-elasticity of covered emissions, 0 when nothing is
  covered;
- $\sigma_s$ is the semi-elasticity of the sector's semi-elasticity group (power, transport, residential, industry;
  legacy table ETS+LTS, by country);
- $\vartheta$ is the effectiveness of output-based allocation (setting `ETSOBREffectiveness`, 0.5): a permit
  allocated free has half the effect of an auctioned one;
- $\hat{p}_t$ (`ets.est`) is the fast estimate of the permit price in USD/tCO2.

**Permit price, tax-equivalent price, revenue factor.**

$$
p^{E}_t = \text{on}_t \begin{cases} \text{override}_t \ (\text{blank: } \tau_t) & \text{ETSPriceOverride = Yes} \\ \hat{p}_t & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}, \qquad \tilde{p}^{E}_t = p^{E}_t\, V, \qquad \rho = \frac{1}{V}
$$ {#eq-ov-ets-price}

where $p^{E}_t$ (`ets.p`, methodology $NETSP$) is the permit price, $\tilde{p}^{E}_t$ (`ets.pe`) the tax-equivalent
price that enters behaviour, and $\rho$ (`ets.rf`) the revenue factor: permit revenue per USD of tax-equivalent
cost. The override row holds prices pasted from the goal seek (@sec-emissions).

**The ETS cost by sector.** The tax-equivalent price splits by the OBR share. The auctioned part enters the fuel
price like a tax; the free part acts only on efficiency, through the shadow price (@eq-ov-shadow):

$$
A_{s,t} = \tilde{p}^{E}_t\;\kappa_{s,t}\;(1 - \omega_{s,t})
$$ {#eq-ov-etr}

where $A_{s,t}$ (`etr`) is the ETS cost in the fuel price of sector $s$, USD/tCO2 ([M1.3](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-3)).
Revenue counts the auctioned part times $\rho$, the permit price; the free part raises none (@sec-fiscal).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: new ETS"}
```
for t in years:
    on[t] = NewETS starts with 'Yes' and t >= ETSIntro
    for s in coverage_sectors:                                   # power + 16 subsectors
        etsc[s][t] = on[t] * ETSCov[s]
    for G in ['pow', 'tra', 'res', 'ind']:
        etsb[G][t] = path(t, ETSIntro, ETSOutro, 1 - ETSAuctStart, 1 - ETSAuctTarget, hold=True)
    for s in coverage_sectors:
        obr[s][t] = clip(etsb[ets_group(s)][t], 0, 1)
    vadj = (1 + ETSCTRisk * imp[ETSVolImpact]) / (1 + vol[ETSVolatility] * imp[ETSVolImpact])
    bce[t] = sum(bco2[s][t] * etsc[s][t] for s in coverage_sectors)     # stored baseline CO2
    chg[t] = path(t, ETSIntro, ETSOutro, ETSChangeRelStart, ETSChangeRelTarget, hold=True)
    cap[t] = on[t] * bce[t] * (1 + chg[t])
    if ETSCapCont starts with 'Constant' and t > ETSOutro:
        cap[t] = cap[t-1] if on[t] else 0
    se[t] = sum(bco2[s][t] * etsc[s][t] * semi[semi_group(s)] * (1 - (1 - obr_eff) * obr[s][t])
                for s in coverage_sectors) / bce[t]   if bce[t] > 0 else 0
    est[t] = log(cap[t] / bce[t]) / (se[t] * vadj)   if on[t] and 0 < cap[t] < bce[t] and se[t] < 0 else 0
    p[t] = (override[t] or cptraj[t]) if ETSPriceOverride starts with 'Yes' else est[t]
    p[t] = p[t] if on[t] else 0
    pe[t] = p[t] * vadj                                         # tax-equivalent price
    rf = 1 / vadj                                               # revenue factor
    for s in coverage_sectors:
        etr[s][t] = pe[t] * etsc[s][t] * (1 - obr[s][t])        # auctioned part, in the fuel price
```
:::

### Feebates and regulations: the shadow price {#sec-ov-shadow}

Feebates and regulations make energy use more efficient without raising the price of energy. A feebate charges
above-average emitters and rebates below-average ones, so it is revenue neutral; a regulation sets a standard. The
model represents both as a **shadow price** per tonne of CO2 that acts only on the efficiency margin of fuel use
(@sec-demand) and on power (@sec-power), and raises no revenue. The user guide describes feebates in
[methodology, section 1.3.2.4.3](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/01_User_Guide.html#feebates) and regulations in
[section 1.3.2.6](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/01_User_Guide.html#regulations-and-subsidies).

**Feebate rates.** One rate per feebate group $G$ (power, transport, residential, industry), linear from
`FeebateIntro` to `FeebateOutro` and held after:

$$
b_{G,t} = \bar{\Lambda}\big(t;\, T^{b}_0, T^{b}_1,\, b_{G,0},\, b_{G,1}\big)
$$ {#eq-ov-feebate}

where $b_{G,t}$ (`fb`) is in USD/tCO2 and $b_{G,0}$, $b_{G,1}$ are `Feb_Level_Start_<group>`,
`Feb_Level_Target_<group>`. Food and forestry and services take the residential rate; other energy use the industry
rate.

**Regulations.** The main scenario (`ScenarioSelected`) decides whether the carbon price path is an explicit tax or
a shadow price, which efficiency adjustment applies and which sectors the shadow price covers:

| Main scenario | Explicit pricing | Efficiency adjustment | Sectors covered by the shadow price |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | No | none (0) | none |
| Carbon tax | Yes | — | — |
| Total carbon price | Yes | — | — |
| Coal excise | Yes | — | — |
| Road fuel tax | Yes | — | — |
| Electricity emissions tax | Yes | — | — |
| Electricity excise | Yes | — | — |
| Feebates; power supply feebates | No | feebates (5) | all |
| Energy efficiency regulations | No | energy efficiency regulations (1) | all |
| Power feebate | No | feebates (5) | power |
| Vehicle fuel economy | No | vehicle fuel economy (2) | road |
| Residential efficiency regulations | No | residential (3) | residential |
| Industrial efficiency regulations | No | industrial (4) | food and forestry, services, industry, other energy use |

The adjustments are the inputs `SPPEffAdjEnergyEfficiencyRegulations` (1), `SPPEffAdjVehicleFuelEconomy` (2),
`SPPEffAdjRes` (3), `SPPEffAdjInd` (4) and `SPPEffAdjFeebates` (5): the share of the shadow price that reaches the
efficiency margin (Egypt: 0.7 for the regulations, 1 for feebates). Under shadow pricing there is no explicit carbon
tax ($\tau^x = 0$), and the carbon price path becomes the shadow carbon price:

$$
\mathit{reg}_{s,t} = (\tau_t - \tau^{x}_t)\; a^{reg}\; \mathbb{1}[\text{main scenario covers } s]
$$ {#eq-ov-reg}

where $\mathit{reg}_{s,t}$ (`reg`) is the regulation shadow price of sector $s$, $\tau_t - \tau^x_t$ the shadow carbon price
(`cp.shd`) and $a^{reg}$ (`regadj`) the efficiency adjustment of the main scenario.

**The shadow price by sector.** Feebates, regulations and the free part of the ETS add up
([M1.4](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-4)):

$$
\Sigma_{s,t} = b_{G(s),t}\; a^{fb}\; \mathbb{1}[\text{feebate covers } s] \;+\; \mathit{reg}_{s,t} \;+\; \tilde{p}^{E}_t\;\kappa_{s,t}\;\omega_{s,t}
$$ {#eq-ov-shadow}

where

- $\Sigma_{s,t}$ (`shpx`) is the shadow price of sector $s$ in USD/tCO2;
- $a^{fb}$ is `SPPEffAdjFeebates`, the share of the feebate on the efficiency margin; the product
  $a^{fb}\,\mathbb{1}[\cdot]$ is `ssc`;
- the feebate coverage switches are `FbCovPow`, ..., `FbCovOen`.

Other regulation inputs act directly on efficiency rather than through a price: the additional policy-induced
efficiency gains `AdditionalEfficiencyRoadVehicle`, `AdditionalEfficiencyResidential`,
`AdditionalEfficiencyIndustrial` (@sec-demand) and `AdditionalEfficiencyPower` (@sec-power). The road engineer
model's vehicle feebate uses the road regulation shadow price (@sec-transport).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: shadow prices"}
```
scn = position of ScenarioSelected in main_scenarios (0 if not found)
explicit = 1 if scn == 0 else main_scenarios[scn].explicit
regadj   = 0 if scn == 0 or main_scenarios[scn].adjustment == 0 \
           else [SPPEffAdjEnergyEfficiencyRegulations, SPPEffAdjVehicleFuelEconomy,
                 SPPEffAdjRes, SPPEffAdjInd, SPPEffAdjFeebates][main_scenarios[scn].adjustment - 1]
for t in years:
    for G in ['pow', 'tra', 'res', 'ind']:
        fb[G][t] = path(t, FeebateIntro, FeebateOutro, fb_start[G], fb_target[G], hold=True)
    cpx[t] = cptraj[t] * explicit
    shadow[t] = cptraj[t] - cpx[t]
    for s in coverage_sectors:
        regc = scn > 0 and main_scenarios[scn].covers[s]
        reg[s][t] = shadow[t] * regadj * regc
        ssc[s] = FbCov[s] * SPPEffAdjFeebates
        shpx[s][t] = fb[feebate_group(s)][t] * ssc[s] + reg[s][t] + ets_pe[t] * etsc[s][t] * obr[s][t]
```
:::

### Fuel excises: the fuel price reform {#sec-ov-excise}

A new excise is a tax per unit of fuel, set in the fuel's own price unit (USD/liter for gasoline, diesel, LPG and
kerosene, USD/bbl for other oil products, USD/GJ for coal, gas and biomass, USD/kWh for electricity). The model calls
it the **fuel price reform**: one increase path per price block, all with the same start and target year
(`FprIntro`, `FprOutro`). The methodology describes new excises in
[methodology, section 3.9.3.1.4](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#policy-options-new-excise-existing-excise-exemptions).

Up to the target year the path is linear; after it, the input `ExtendCarbonPriceBeyondOutro` (the same as for the
carbon price) chooses how it continues ([M1.5](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-5)):

$$
F_{g,f,t} = \begin{cases} 0 & t < T^{F}_0 \\[2pt] x_0 + j\,(t - T^{F}_0) & t < T^{F}_1 \text{ or Linear*} \\[2pt] \hat{x}\,(1 + k)^{\,t - T^{F}_1 + 1} & \text{Percentage} \\[2pt] x_1 & \text{otherwise (held)} \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ov-fpr}

with

$$
j = \frac{x_1 - x_0}{T^{F}_1 - T^{F}_0}, \qquad k = \left(\frac{x_1}{x_0}\right)^{1/(T^{F}_1 - T^{F}_0)} - 1, \qquad \hat{x} = x_0 + j\,\max(T^{F}_1 - T^{F}_0 - 1,\, 0)
$$ {#eq-ov-fpr-parts}

where

- $F_{g,f,t}$ (`fpr`) is the excise increase of price block $(g,f)$ in its price unit;
- $x_0$, $x_1$ are the start and final increases (`FprStart<Fuel><Sector>`, `FprFinal<Fuel><Sector>`);
- $j$ (`fprj`) is the annual step, 0 if the target year is not after the start year;
- $k$ (`fprk`) is the average annual growth rate of the path; where the start is zero it divides by $x_0 + j$
  instead of $x_0$; it is 0 if both levels are zero or the years do not increase;
- $\hat{x}$ (`fprp`) is the value of the year before the target year; the value after the target year is `fpra`;
- if the target year is not after the start year, the held value is $x_0$.

**The new excise of a price block.** The gross new excise (`ntxg`) is the reform path, plus the Pigouvian tax when
`AddEfficientTaxes` = Yes (@sec-ov-pigouvian). It applies in policy scenarios only:

$$
N^{x}_{g,f,t} = \mathbb{1}[o \ne B]\; F_{g,f,t}
$$ {#eq-ov-ntxb}

(`ntxb`). Prices divide it by the GJ per price unit and multiply it by the exemption factor $x_{s,f}$ to get the new
excise per GJ of each subsector (@sec-prices). The electricity blocks reach the electricity price through the power
block, together with the manual electricity excise of `AdditionalExcise` ([A4.7](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A4-7),
@sec-power).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: fuel price reform"}
```
for (g, f) in price_blocks + [('res', 'ecy'), ('ind', 'ecy')]:      # 14 blocks
    s0, s1 = FprStart[g, f], FprFinal[g, f]
    j = (s1 - s0) / (FprOutro - FprIntro) if FprOutro > FprIntro else 0
    k = 0
    if FprOutro > FprIntro and max(s0, s1) > 0:
        k = (s1 / (s0 if s0 > 0 else s0 + j)) ** (1 / (FprOutro - FprIntro)) - 1
    before_target = s0 + j * max(FprOutro - FprIntro - 1, 0)
    for t in years:
        if ExtendCarbonPriceBeyondOutro == 'Percentage':
            after = before_target * (1 + k) ** (t - FprOutro + 1)
        else:
            after = s1 if FprOutro > FprIntro else s0
        if t < FprIntro:
            fpr[g, f][t] = 0
        elif t < FprOutro or ExtendCarbonPriceBeyondOutro == 'Linear*':
            fpr[g, f][t] = s0 + j * (t - FprIntro)
        else:
            fpr[g, f][t] = after
        ntxg[g, f][t] = fpr[g, f][t]                    # + Pigouvian tax if AddEfficientTaxes (Excel-AI only)
        ntxb[g, f][t] = ntxg[g, f][t] * (scenario > 1)
```
:::

### Subsidy and price-control phase-outs {#sec-ov-phaseouts}

Many countries subsidise fuels, either explicitly (a consumer or producer subsidy) or by controlling the retail price
so that it does not follow the supply cost. The model can phase out three kinds of support, each with its own switch,
start year, period and share: **producer subsidies**, **consumer subsidies** and **price controls**. The
methodology describes these reforms in
[methodology, section 3.9.3.1.6](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#fossil-fuel-subsidies-reform)
and [section 3.9.3.1.7](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#price-liberalization).

**The phase-out factor.** For each phase-out $k$, the share of the original support still in place
([M1.7](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-7)):

$$
\phi_{k,t} = \max\!\left(1 - \bar{s}_k,\;\; \begin{cases} 1 - \bar{s}_k\,\dfrac{t - T_k}{\max(N_k, 1)} & \text{on}_k \text{ and } t > T_k \\[6pt] 1 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\right)
$$ {#eq-ov-pof}

where

- $\phi_{k,t}$ (`pof`) is the share of the original subsidy (or floating tax) kept, from 1 down to $1 - \bar{s}_k$;
- $T_k$ is the start year (`YearProdSubPha`, `YearConsSubPha`, `YearPrcContPha`);
- $N_k$ (`po.n`) is the phase-out period in years, $\bar{s}_k$ (`po.sh`) the share phased out, and
  $\text{on}_k$ (`po.on`) whether the phase-out applies.

The baseline can phase out subsidies too (a reform already decided). The baseline and policy scenarios read
different inputs:

| | Producer subsidies | Consumer subsidies | Price controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| On, baseline | `ProdSubPhaBaseline` | `ConsSubPhaBaseline` | `PrcContPha` and `PrcContPhaBaseline` |
| On, policy scenario | `ProdSubPh` | `ConsSubPha` | `PrcContPha` |
| Period, baseline | `FFSProdPhaseoutPeriodBA` | `FFSConsPhaseoutPeriodBA` | `PrcControlPhaseout` |
| Period, policy scenario | `FFSProdPhaseoutPeriod` | `FFPhaseOut` | `PrcControlPhaseout` |
| Share, baseline | `ShareOfProdSubPhaBA` | `ShareofConsSubPhaBA` | as consumer subsidies |
| Share, policy scenario | larger of `ShareOfProdSubPhaBA`, `ShareofProdSubPha` | larger of `ShareofConsSubPhaBA`, `ShareOfConsSubPha` | as consumer subsidies |

A switch counts as on when it is TRUE or starts with "Yes". Price controls are phased out only where the policy
switch is on (and, in the baseline, the baseline switch too), and they use the consumer-subsidy shares (issue I48).

**Scope by fuel and sector.** Scope switches let a reform cover some price blocks or fuels only:

$$
cs_{g,f,t} = 1 - i^{cs}_{g,f}\,(1 - \phi_{cs,t}), \qquad pc_{g,f,t} = 1 - i^{pc}_{g,f}\,(1 - \phi_{pc,t}), \qquad \mathit{ps}_{f,t} = 1 - i^{ps}_{f}\,(1 - \phi_{ps,t})
$$ {#eq-ov-scope}

where

- $cs$ (`csf`), $pc$ (`pcf`) are the consumer-subsidy and price-control factors of each of the 12 fuel price
  blocks, and $ps$ (`psf`) the producer-subsidy factor of each producer fuel (coal, gas, oil, biomass,
  electricity);
- $i^{cs}$, $i^{pc}$, $i^{ps}$ (`csi`, `pci`, `psi`) are the scope switches (`ConsSubPhaseScope_<fuel>_<sector>`,
  `PriceCtrlPhaseScope_<fuel>_<sector>`, `ProdSubPhaseScope_<fuel>`), 1 where the reform applies.

The factors become **wedges** in the after-tax price: the consumer-subsidy reform removes part of the fixed
subsidy, the price-control phase-out part of the floating tax or subsidy that absorbs supply-cost changes
(@sec-prices). The saved subsidy is revenue (@sec-fiscal). Subsidy reforms of electricity prices are part of the
power block (@sec-power).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: phase-out factors"}
```
for k in ['ps', 'cs', 'pc']:
    if k == 'pc':
        on = PrcContPha and (scenario > 1 or PrcContPhaBaseline)
        share = ShareofConsSubPhaBA if scenario == 1 else max(ShareofConsSubPhaBA, ShareOfConsSubPha)
    else:
        on = baseline_switch[k] if scenario == 1 else policy_switch[k]
        share = share_BA[k] if scenario == 1 else max(share_BA[k], share_policy[k])
    period = period_BA[k] if scenario == 1 else period_policy[k]
    for t in years:
        pof[k][t] = max(1 - share,
                        1 - share * (t - start_year[k]) / max(period, 1) if on and t > start_year[k] else 1)
for (g, f) in price_blocks:                                  # 12 blocks
    csf[g, f] = 1 - csi[g, f] * (1 - pof['cs'])
    pcf[g, f] = 1 - pci[g, f] * (1 - pof['pc'])
for f in ['coa', 'nga', 'oil', 'bio', 'ecy']:
    psf[f] = 1 - psi[f] * (1 - pof['ps'])
```
:::

### Producer subsidy reform {#sec-ov-producer}

A producer subsidy lowers the cost of supplying a fuel. The model reads the subsidy of each fuel from the price data,
spreads it over the demand it supports to get a subsidy per unit, and lowers it with the producer phase-out factor
after the last historical price year ([A2.5](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A2-5)):

$$
\mathit{ps}_{f,t} = \begin{cases} -\dfrac{\mathit{PROS}_{f,t}}{D_{f,t}} & t \le L \\[8pt] \mathit{ps}_{f,L}\;\mathit{ps}^{\phi}_{f,t} & t > L \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ov-producer}

where

- $\mathit{ps}_{f,t}$ (`psu`) is the producer subsidy per unit of fuel $f$ (negative: USD/liter for oil, USD/GJ for coal,
  gas and biomass);
- $\mathit{PROS}_{f,t}$ (`pros`) is the producer subsidy (price data, USD billion nominal, times the CPI index and 1000:
  USD million real; held after $L$), times $10^6$ to get USD;
- $D_{f,t}$ (`psd`) is the demand that carries the subsidy: world demand times liters per ktoe for oil; the average
  of world demand and domestic consumption (excluding electricity and heat) times GJ per ktoe for coal and gas;
  domestic consumption times GJ per ktoe for biomass;
- $\mathit{ps}^{\phi}_{f,t}$ is the producer-subsidy factor `psf` of @eq-ov-scope.

The per-unit subsidy enters the supply cost of each price block of the fuel, so the floating taxes and price controls
absorb part of a phase-out, as in legacy (@sec-prices). The subsidy itself is a fiscal line (`rpsu`, @sec-fiscal).
The electricity producer subsidy is allocated between user groups in the power block (@sec-power).

### Methane fee {#sec-ov-methane}

The methane fee is a charge per tonne of CO2-equivalent of methane from the sources it covers (fuel supply, gas
distribution, agriculture, waste). It drives methane abatement and raises revenue (@sec-emissions, @sec-fiscal).
The methodology describes methane in
[methodology, section 3.5.4.2](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#methane-ch_4).

$$
m_t = \Lambda\big(t;\, T^{m}_0, T^{m}_1, m_0, m_1\big)\;\mathbb{1}[o \ne B] \;+\; \tau_t\;\mathbb{1}[\text{carbon tax applies to methane}]
$$ {#eq-ov-mfee}

where

- $m_t$ (`mfee`) is the methane fee in USD/tCO2e; the path alone is `mfee.p`;
- $T^{m}_0$, $T^{m}_1$, $m_0$, $m_1$ are `MPIntro`, `MPOutro`, `MPLevelStart`, `MPLevelTarget`; the path
  continues linearly after the target year;
- the fee path applies only in policy scenarios; the carbon price $\tau_t$ is added in any scenario where
  `CTforMethane` = Yes ([M1.8](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-8)).

Which methane sources the fee covers is set by switches per source (Excel-AI sheet Manual inputs; @sec-emissions).

### Existing carbon pricing {#sec-ov-existing}

Some countries already price carbon. The IMF retail prices contain whatever existing carbon pricing the country had
in the price data, so the model adds only the **change** against that level: a scheme switched off lowers the price
by its embedded level, growth or new data raise it. The data are the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard and ICAP
(legacy sheet ECP, as of 1 April 2025; 52 countries). The methodology describes the options in
[methodology, section 3.9.3.1.3](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#policy-options-existing-carbon-pricing-policies).

**Data by ECP sector and fuel.** For each ECP sector $j$ (power, transport, residential, industry), fuel $f$ and
data year $y$ (2021 to $T_x = 2025$), in real USD/tCO2:

$$
XT_{j,f,y} = r_{f,y}\; sc_{j,y}\; fc_{f,y}, \qquad XE_{j,f,y} = p^{nat}_y\; n_{j,y}\; nf_{f,y} \;+\; p^{EU}_y\; e_{j,y}\; ef^{EU}_{f,y}
$$ {#eq-ov-ecp-data}

where

- $XT$ is the existing carbon tax and $XE$ the existing ETS price of the sector and fuel;
- $r_{f,y}$ is the carbon tax rate of the fuel where the country has fuel rates and no "single price" flag,
  otherwise the single rate; $sc$, $fc$ its sector and fuel coverage;
- $p^{nat}$ is the national ETS price with coverage $n$, $nf$; $p^{EU}$ the EU ETS price with the country's
  regional coverage $e$, $ef^{EU}$, counted only if the country is in the EU ETS (flag Yes or Both);
- prices are made real with the CPI index of the data year; blank coverage is 0.

**Scenario factors.** Each scheme can be switched off or grown after the last data year:

$$
\phi^{ct}_t = \mathbb{1}[\text{ExistingCTApply}]\,(1 + \gamma^{ct})^{\max(0,\, t - T_x)}, \qquad \phi^{ets}_t = \mathbb{1}[\text{ExistingETSApply}]\,(1 + \gamma^{ets})^{\max(0,\, t - T_x)}
$$ {#eq-ov-ecp-factors}

where $\phi^{ct}$ (`xct.p`), $\phi^{ets}$ (`xets.p`) multiply the data of year $t^* = \min(t, T_x)$ (`xct.c`), and
$\gamma^{ct}$, $\gamma^{ets}$ are `ExistingCTGrowth`, `ExistingETSGrowth`. The level per GJ is then the emission
factor times $XT\,\phi^{ct} + XE\,\phi^{ets}$; the price block takes the change against the level embedded in the
price data, of year $\min(L, T_x)$ ([A2.2](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A2-2), @sec-prices). The change also enters the
variable cost of power plants (@sec-power).

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode: existing carbon pricing"}
```
eu = country in EU ETS ('Yes' or 'Both')
for y in [2021, ..., 2025]:
    for f in fuels:
        rate[f][y] = single_rate[y] if single_price or no fuel rate else fuel_rate[f][y]
        rate[f][y] *= infl[y]                                         # real USD of the results year
    for j in ['pow', 'trs', 'res', 'ind']:
        for f in fuels:
            xct[j, f][y] = rate[f][y] * tax_sector_cov[j][y] * tax_fuel_cov[f][y]
            xets[j, f][y] = (nat_price[y] * infl[y] * nat_sector_cov[j][y] * nat_fuel_cov[f][y]
                             + eu * eu_price[y] * infl[y] * eu_sector_cov[j][y] * eu_fuel_cov[f][y])
for t in years:
    xct_c[t] = column of min(t, 2025)
    xct_p[t] = (1 + ExistingCTGrowth) ** max(0, t - 2025) if ExistingCTApply starts with 'Yes' else 0
    xets_p[t] = (1 + ExistingETSGrowth) ** max(0, t - 2025) if ExistingETSApply starts with 'Yes' else 0
```
:::

### Social cost of carbon {#sec-ov-scc}

The social cost of carbon values a tonne of CO2. It does not change behaviour by itself: it is used by the climate
part of the Pigouvian tax (@sec-ov-pigouvian) and by the welfare results (@sec-fiscal). The methodology discusses it
in [methodology, section 3.7](../CPAT_full_documentation_html/03_Mitigation.html#monetized-social-costs-and-benefits).
Five paths are computed, each growing at the rate $g^{scc}$ ([M1.6](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-M1-6)):

$$
\mathit{SCC}^{tgt}_t = \mathit{SCC}^{*}\,(1 + g^{scc})^{t - T^{*}}, \qquad \mathit{SCC}^{x}_t = \mathit{SCC}^{x}\,(1 + g^{scc})^{t - t_0} \quad (x = \text{Ricke national, Ricke global, EPA})
$$ {#eq-ov-scc}

| Path | Value | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Target-consistent price $\mathit{SCC}^{*}$ in year $T^{*}$ | `SCCTargetConsistentCP`, `SCCTargetYear` | 75 USD/tCO2 in 2030 |
| Ricke et al. (2018), national and global | Sheet SCC, by discount rate `NSCCDiscountRate` and elasticity `NSCCMargUtilofCons` | 2%, 1.5% |
| Manual | Data path by year | — |
| US EPA | `SCCEpaBaseYear` in the base year | 62 USD/tCO2 |
| Growth rate $g^{scc}$ | `SCCRise` | 4% per year |

The national and the global SCC are each chosen by `NSCCSource` and `GSCCSource` (by first letter: Target, Ricke,
Manual, US EPA; default Target*). These settings are read from the baseline column.

### Pigouvian (efficient) taxes {#sec-ov-pigouvian}

With `AddEfficientTaxes` = Yes, the new excise of each price block adds a **Pigouvian tax**: the external cost of a
unit of fuel that its price does not already cover ([A1.2](A_Equations.qmd#eqlist-A1-2)). It has three parts:

- **air pollution:** the value of averted PM2.5 (from the air pollution module) times the module's concentration
  coefficients of the source times the combustion factors of the fuel, per GJ, weighted by base-year fuel use
  (residential coal only where coal is above `ApCoalResMin`, 0.1% of buildings fuel use);
- **climate** (if `ClimateEffTax`): the national SCC times the generic CO2 factor of the fuel;
- **road transport:** accident, congestion and road-damage costs per km (from the transport co-benefits module),
  converted per unit of fuel with base-year fuel economy, the elasticity share of usage and the road share of the
  fuel.

The sum is phased in over `AddEfficientTaxesPhaseInYears` from `CPIntro`. Where an existing pre-tax wedge already
covers part of it, the new excise is $\min\big(n,\ \max(0,\ n - w\,\gamma)\big)$, with $n$ the gross excise, $w$ the
existing wedge per GJ and $\gamma$ the GJ per price unit (issue I113). The module values enter in the prepare stage,
so the Pigouvian tax is exogenous to the year loop (issue I151).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python"}
- **Excel-AI:** sheet Mitigation, section 1 (rows of `Formulas.md` E7-E235): the input rows read from
  ScenarioDefinition, then the carbon price (`cp.t`, `cp.nom`, `exph`, `ctcov`, `cptraj`), fuel price reform
  (`fprj` ... `fpr`), SCC (`scc`), Pigouvian taxes (rows 185-418: `pig.*`, `airpol.mc`, `cc.code`, `pigx`, `ntxg`,
  `xcpb`, `xpre`, `ntxb`), new ETS (`ets.on` ... `ets.rf`), feebates (`fb`, `fbcov`), main scenario (`scn`,
  `cp.exp`, `cpx`, `cp.shd`, `regadj`, `regc`, `reg`, `ssc`), sector rates (`ctr`, `etr`, `shpx`), existing carbon
  pricing (`xct.c`, `xct.p`, `xets.p`), phase-outs (`po.on` ... `psu`), `exf`, methane fee (`mfee.p`, `mfee`).
  Data: sheet Inputs_ecp (existing carbon pricing), BaselineCO2 (`bco2`, `ch4bs` from scenario 1), ETSSemi
  (semi-elasticities), SCC; the volatility table and `ETSOBREffectiveness` on Settings; the main-scenario table on
  sheet Mapping.
- **CPAT Python:** `cpat_model/mitigation/policies.py`, `prepare()`: equations M1.1-M1.8, A1.1 and the factors of
  A2.2; `linear_path()` is M1.1. The Pigouvian rows are in `pigouvian.py`, `prepare()` (A1.2); the producer
  subsidies (`pros`, `psd`, `psu`, A2.5) in the prices block. The tables `main_scenarios.csv`,
  `ets_volatility.csv`, `coverage_sectors.csv` and `input_rows.csv` are in `core/excel_ai/`; the stored baseline CO2
  in `data/<edition>/inputs/baseline_co2.csv`.
- **Not in CPAT Python yet:** `AddEfficientTaxes` = Yes (the run stops with an error); the ETS override row (with
  `ETSPriceOverride` = Yes the permit price is the carbon price path); the initially exempt cooking fuel
  (`ExemptMostCook` = Yes, @sec-demand).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT"}
Legacy bugs (L) are fixed; issues (I) are replicated; departures (LD) are recorded decisions.

| Code | Area | What the model does |
|---|---|---|
| LD10, L171, L173, L174 | Paths after the target year | Carbon price per its switch; fuel price reform Linear*, Percentage or held (legacy did not hold the target under No, L171, and lacked the 1 + rate, L173); feebates held (L174); ETS benchmarks constant; ETS cap per its switch |
| L94 | Exemption phase-out | One rule for every coverage row (legacy chose it row by row) |
| LD13 | Biomass coverage | Biomass is covered by the carbon tax (emission factor 0), a decision |
| LD6, L15, L16 | ETS price | Fast estimate in log form with the volatility adjustment in place of legacy's hardcoded 1.1 and linear form; baseline covered emissions are scenario-1 data; override pasted from the goal seek |
| LD7, I21, L78 | ETS allocation | One auctioned share for every group, as legacy (I21); benchmark = 1 − auctioned share, held after the target year (legacy dropped it to 0 unless the cap is Constant, L78) |
| LD8 | ETS volatility | Volatility adjustment from the inputs, applied to the tax-equivalent price and the fast estimate |
| LD9, L87, L88, M13 | Regulations | The main scenario sets explicit or shadow pricing, as legacy, with legacy's bugs fixed: legacy's regulation share was 0 (L87) and never reached power (L88); the road vehicle feebate uses the regulation shadow price, not the carbon price already in the fuel price (prototype bug M13) |
| LD12 | Feebate groups | Food and forestry and services take the residential rate, other energy use the industry rate, as legacy |
| LD18, L81, I48 | Subsidy and price-control phase-outs | Separate lines by price block and sector, as legacy; the same year for every line (legacy lags the fixed subsidy a year, L81); price controls use the consumer shares (I48) |
| LD19, L124, L125 | Producer subsidies | In the supply cost as legacy, per unit and phased out by `psf`; legacy read the oil value for residential gas (L124) and added a per-liter value to the per-barrel price of other oil products (L125) |
| L61-L65 | Existing carbon pricing | Fixed: the EU ETS grew with the carbon-tax growth (L61); transport diesel, LPG and kerosene took the rate as coverage (L62); a fuel coverage lookup stopped short (L63); no ETS on other oil products outside power (L64); the complementary tax used last year's coverage (L65) |
| LD46 | Methane fee | Fee only in policy scenarios, as legacy; scope switches per source |
| I113, I151 | Pigouvian taxes | New excise net of existing wedges (I113); module values exogenous, in the prepare stage (I151) |
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check: results for Egypt"}
The policies block matches Excel-AI's stored values for Egypt in every scenario and year (CPAT Python test block
"3.2 policies"; no known differences). Egypt has no existing carbon pricing and no producer subsidy data. Values of
the shipped scenario set:

| Scenario | Inputs | 2026 | 2027 | 2030 | 2035 | 2041 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2: carbon price USD 20 from 2027 | `cptraj` (USD/tCO2) | 0 | 20 | 20 | 20 | 20 |
| 4: package A, transport feebate USD 10 (2027) to 50 (2030) | `fb` transport | 0 | 10 | 50 | 50 | 50 |
| 5: package B, ETS cap −5% (2027) to −20% (2035), constant after | `ets.bce` (MtCO2) | 0 | 120.84 | 130.29 | 132.49 | 142.57 |
| | `ets.cap` (MtCO2) | 0 | 114.80 | 116.45 | 105.99 | 105.99 |
| | `ets.se` (per USD/tCO2) | 0 | −0.001574 | −0.001579 | −0.001604 | −0.001623 |
| | `ets.p` fast estimate (USD/tCO2) | 0 | 35.86 | 78.26 | 153.04 | 200.93 |
| | `ets.pe` tax-equivalent (USD/tCO2) | 0 | 32.60 | 71.15 | 139.13 | 182.67 |

The volatility adjustment is $V = 0.9091$ (Medium). For 2027: $\ln(114.80/120.84) = -0.0513$, divided by
$-0.001574 \times 0.9091$, gives 35.86 USD/tCO2. The feebate is held at its target after 2030; the cap is held at its
2035 level while the baseline covered emissions keep growing, so the estimated price keeps rising.
:::

### Coverage by fuel and sector: summary {#sec-ov-coverage}

Each instrument has its own coverage, set by its own switches.

| Instrument | Coverage by fuel | Coverage by sector | Exemptions and phase-in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Carbon tax | `MCovCoa` ... `MCovOop`, `CTaxCoversBiomass` (jet fuel: kerosene switch) | `MCovPow` ... `MCovOen` (17) | Exemption phase-out (`ExemptPhaseout`); residential LPG and kerosene (`AlwaysExemptResLPGKer`); complementary to an existing ETS |
| New ETS | All fossil fuels of a covered sector | `ETSCovPow` ... `ETSCovOen` (17) | The ETS replaces the carbon tax where it covers; free allocation by group |
| Feebates | All fuels of a covered sector | `FbCovPow` ... `FbCovOen` (17) | Rates by group: power, transport, residential, industry |
| Regulations | All fuels of a covered sector | Set by the main scenario | Efficiency adjustment of the main scenario |
| Fuel price reform | One path per price block (14) | Price sector of the block | Residential LPG and kerosene exemption; policy scenarios only |
| Consumer subsidy, price-control phase-outs | Scope switches per price block (12) | Price sector of the block | Baseline or policy inputs |
| Producer subsidy reform | Scope switches per producer fuel (5) | All sectors (through the supply cost) | Baseline or policy inputs |
| Methane fee | Methane sources by switch | — | Policy scenarios only (plus the carbon price if `CTforMethane`) |
| Existing carbon pricing | Data by fuel | Data by ECP sector (4) | Switch per scheme |

The household initially exempt from the price of its most-used cooking fuel (`ExemptMostCook`) is a demand-side
exemption, explained in @sec-demand.

## How to read the rest of this book {#sec-ov-reading}

The chapters follow the order of the calculation chain. Each one opens with what its block computes and why it
matters, then gives the equations, then the details.

| Chapter | What it explains |
|---|---|
| @sec-prices | International prices, supply costs, existing taxes and subsidies, VAT, and the after-tax and shadow prices into which the policies of this chapter enter |
| @sec-demand | Fuel use by subsector and fuel: income, price and efficiency elasticities, biofuels, leakage to biomass, energy totals |
| @sec-power | Electricity demand, dispatch, retirement, investment, storage, generation costs, electricity prices and power-sector policies |
| @sec-transport | The road engineer model: vehicle stocks, cost of ownership, the choice between combustion and electric vehicles, vehicle policies |
| @sec-emissions | CO2, the ETS cap check and goal seek, other greenhouse gases and methane, local air pollutants, the NDC gap |
| @sec-fiscal | Revenues, the fiscal space and its uses, multipliers and the GDP feedback, welfare |
| @sec-distribution | Household effects by decile in the analysis year: direct and indirect price effects, revenue recycling |

Two appendices list every equation of the model, in calculation order, with the ids the chapters cite:

- @sec-eqlist gives them in the notation of the CPAT methodology;
- @sec-eqcodes gives the same equations with the CPAT variable codes that Excel-AI rows and CPAT Python variables
  use.

**The four kinds of box.** Every chapter uses the same four boxes:

::: {.callout-tip icon=false title="Pseudocode (open)"}
The computation of the section in Python-like pseudocode, with the CPAT variable codes and explicit loops over
years, fuels and types. It is the same for Excel-AI and CPAT Python.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In Excel-AI and CPAT Python (collapsed)"}
Where the equations live: the Excel-AI sheet, section and inputs; the CPAT Python module, function and equation ids.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="Differences from legacy CPAT (collapsed)"}
Legacy bugs fixed (L), issues replicated (I), recorded departures (LD) and bugs of earlier prototype versions (M),
with their codes from the register.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check: results for Egypt (collapsed)"}
Validation: how the block compares with Excel-AI's stored values and with legacy runs, with numbers for Egypt.
:::
